title: Complements of ample divisors are affine
statement:
Let $X$ be a proper scheme over a field $k$, $D\subseteq X$ an
effective Cartier divisor ([def-sc-effective-cartier-divisor]; for $X$ of any dimension: the closed subscheme
whose ideal sheaf $\mathcal I_D$ is an effective Cartier ideal [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal])
and $\mathcal L:=\mathcal O_X(D)=\mathcal I_D^\vee$ ([def-pc-divisor-line-bundle])
ample ([def-sc-ample]). Then $X\setminus D$ is affine.

proof.text: *$X\setminus D=X_s$ for a section $s$ of $\mathcal L$.* By [lem-sc-canonical-section-zero-scheme] there is $s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L)$ (the canonical section $1_D$) with zero scheme $Z(s)=D$. For a global section $t$ of an invertible module $\mathcal M$ write $X_t=\{x\in X:\ t_x\notin\mathfrak m_x\mathcal M_x\}$ as in [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. $\mathcal L$ is invertible [lem-pc-divisor-line-bundle-invertible], so $X$ is covered by affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ on which $\mathcal L$ is free on a generator $e$ [def-sc-invertible-module]; write $s|_U=a\,e$ with $a\in A$. By [lem-pc-zero-scheme-properties] (1), $Z(s)\cap U=\operatorname{Spec}(A/(a))$, whose underlying set is $V(a)=\{\mathfrak p: a\in\mathfrak p\}$. For $x\in U$ with prime $\mathfrak p_x$, $e_x$ is a basis of the free rank-one $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module $\mathcal L_x$ and $s_x=a\,e_x$, so $s_x\in\mathfrak m_x\mathcal L_x$ iff $a\in\mathfrak m_x$ iff $a\in\mathfrak p_x$. Hence $X_s\cap U=U\setminus Z(s)$ for every such $U$, and $X_s=X\setminus Z(s)=X\setminus D$ as sets, $X_s$ being open.

source.place: ## Proof, first paragraph: 'Let $s=1_D\in H^0(X,\mathcal L)$ be the canonical section, with $V(s)=D$'; Stacks Divisors 01WX (2), 01X0, 02OQ

proof.text: *$X_{s^{\otimes m}}=X_s$ for $m\ge1$.* On an affine open $U$ as in step 1, $\mathcal L^{\otimes m}|_U$ is free on $e^{\otimes m}$ and $s^{\otimes m}|_U=a^m e^{\otimes m}$; by the computation of step 1, $x\in X_{s^{\otimes m}}$ iff $a^m\notin\mathfrak p_x$, iff $a\notin\mathfrak p_x$ ($\mathfrak p_x$ prime), iff $x\in X_s$. As these $U$ cover $X$, $X_{s^{\otimes m}}=X_s$ (this is the remark $X_{s^n}=X_s$ of Stacks Properties, proof of Lemma 01PT).

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PT (label lemma-ample-power-ample), proof: 'This follows from the fact that $X_{s^n}=X_s$'; the blueprint's '$s^{\otimes m}$ has zero locus $D$'

proof.text: *The embedding by the complete linear system, in coordinates adapted to $s^{\otimes m}$.* By [def-sc-ample] choose $m\ge1$ with $\mathcal L^{\otimes m}$ very ample: with $V=H^0(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes m})$, the complete linear system $|\mathcal L^{\otimes m}|=\mathbf P(V^\vee)$ gives a closed immersion $X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P(V^\vee)\cong\mathbf P^N_k$, $N+1=\dim_kV$, pulling $\mathcal O(1)$ back to $\mathcal L^{\otimes m}$ and the linear forms ($=V$) to the corresponding sections. Put $t=s^{\otimes m}\in V$. If $t=0$ then $X_t=\emptyset$ (a zero section lies in $\mathfrak m_x\mathcal L^{\otimes m}_x$ everywhere), and by steps 1-2 $X\setminus D=X_t=\emptyset$ is affine; so assume $t\ne0$. Choose a basis $t_0=t,t_1,\dots,t_N$ of $V$ and use the dual coordinates $T_0,\dots,T_N$ on $\mathbf P(V^\vee)$, so that the linear form $T_j$ pulls back to $t_j$ (this is the blueprint's linear form $\ell=T_0$ with $i^*\ell=s^{\otimes m}$). In these coordinates the morphism of the complete linear system is the morphism $\varphi=\varphi_{f,(\mathcal L^{\otimes m},(t_0,\dots,t_N))}:X\to\mathbf P^N_k=\mathbf P(\{0,\dots,N\};\operatorname{Spec}k)$ 'given on coordinates by $(t_0:\dots:t_N)$' of [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections] ($f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ the structure morphism; that the complete linear system defines a morphism means that the $t_j$ have no common zero, i.e. generate $\mathcal L^{\otimes m}$ [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-generating-sections-fibre]), and very ampleness says that $\varphi$ is a closed immersion.

source.place: ## Proof, first paragraph: 'Choose $m\geq1$ with $\mathcal L^{\otimes m}$ very ample ... there is a linear form $\ell$ on $\mathbf P^N$ with $i^*\ell=s^{\otimes m}$'

proof.text: *$X_t$ is affine.* By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-morphism-chart-preimage] (i) (with $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $g=f$, $Y=X$ and the sections $t_0,\dots,t_N$), $\varphi^{-1}(D_+(T_0)_k)=X_{t_0}=X_t$: the preimage of the complement of the hyperplane $H=V(T_0)$ is the non-vanishing locus of $t$. By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts] (c) (with $S'=S=\operatorname{Spec}k$), $D_+(T_0)_k$ is affine, $\cong\operatorname{Spec}k[U_1,\dots,U_N]=\mathbf A^N_k$. Since $\varphi$ is a closed immersion, by the affine form of [def-weil-closed-immersion] (Stacks 01QO) the preimage of the affine open $D_+(T_0)_k=\operatorname{Spec}R$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$ for an ideal $I\subseteq R$; so $X_t=\varphi^{-1}(D_+(T_0)_k)$ is affine.

source.place: ## Proof: 'For the hyperplane $H:=V(\ell)$ one has $i^{-1}(H)=V(s^{\otimes m})=D$' and second paragraph: 'The complement of a hyperplane is affine space ... $i(X)\cap\mathbf A^N$ is closed in $\mathbf A^N$, hence affine'

proof.text: *Conclusion.* By steps 1, 2 and 4, $X\setminus D=X_s=X_{s^{\otimes m}}=X_t$ is affine (the case $t=0$ was settled in step 3).

source.place: ## Proof, last sentence: 'therefore $X\setminus D$ is affine'
